subStrands.name: Trust

outcomes.text: emulate Joseph by resisting sexual temptations as young people
exercise assertiveness in the face of temptations/tempting situations
identify people he/she can trust for own safety
recite Psalm 125:1 and trust in God always

learningExperiences: in turns, read Genesis 39:7-12 and retell the story of Joseph and Potiphar’s wife
list lessons learnt from the story of Joseph and Potiphar’s wife
list people they can trust at home, school and in the community
brainstorm on how to escape/avoid temptations/tempting situations
in pairs, roleplay saying No! to sexual temptations
in groups, discuss whom to report to when in danger
write a poem on, ‘People I trust’
role-play saying, ‘No’ to strangers to avoid child abuse or kidnap
list the importance of trusting God
sing a song about trusting God
keyInquiryQuestions: Whom do you trust at home and school?
Why should you avoid talking to strangers?
Why should you put your trust in God?
coreCompetencies: Self-efficacy: the skill of expressing their needs clearly for help is portrayed as learners list people they can trust at home, school and the community.
Creativity and Imagination: the skill of coming up with unique and new ideas is exhibited as learners role-play saying, No! to strangers to avoid child abuse or kidnap.
values: Responsibility: learners observe safety precautions as they say No! to strangers.
pcis: Developmental Perspective: learners learn how to detect, deter and escape from harmful strangers or relatives.
links: English: the skill of writing is applied as learners write a poem.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing a song about trusting God.

subStrands.name: Truthfulness

outcomes.text: state the importance of telling the truth
resist lying as cited in Proverbs 12:19
desire to always speak the truth according to Ephesians 4:25

learningExperiences: read Ephesians 4:25
say why they should always tell the truth
in pairs, say when they did not tell the truth and how to overcome lies
write a poem on the importance of always telling the truth
write Proverbs 12:19 on flash cards and recite it
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you always tell the truth?
coreCompetencies: Imagination and Creativity: the skill of coming up with new ideas and originality is enhanced as they write a poem on the importance of always telling the truth.
Communication and collaboration: the skill of speaking clearly and effectively is enhanced as learners, in pairs, say when they did not tell the truth and how to overcome lies.
values: Integrity: learners say why they should always tell the truth.
pcis: Social Cohesion is portrayed as learners resist lying by always telling the truth.
links: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners write a poem.
English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read and recite Bible texts.

practise responsibility by obeying school rules

desire to exercise obedience in day-to-day life

learningExperiences: read Exodus 20:12 and state the benefit of honouring parents

say why they should obey school rules

coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: the skill of carrying out activities with peers is portrayed as learners list the results of disobedience.
Creativity and Imagination: the skill of coming up with new ideas is nurtured as learners compose a poem on the benefits of obeying parents and teachers.
values: Responsibility: learners obey parents and teachers.
pcis: Peace Education: learners contribute to peace at home by obeying their parents.
links: English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners recite poems.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing a song on the benefits of obedience.

subStrands.name: Love

appreciate God’s love by obeying His teachings

learningExperiences: in groups, retell Jesus Christ’s love for children
role-play Jesus blessing Children (Mathew 19:13-15)
draw Jesus praying for children
watch a video clip on Jesus Christ blessing children
show love to others as taught by Jesus Christ
keyInquiryQuestions: How did Jesus Christ show love to children?
How do you show Godly love to others as a Christian?

Digital Literacy: the skill of digital citizenship is portrayed as learners watch a video clip on Jesus Christ blessing children.

Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners draw and role play.

subStrands.name: Responsibility: Personal and school items

acquire responsibility by taking care of personal and school properties

learningExperiences: display personal items e.g. pullover, pen, pencils, eraser, exercise books, text books
in pairs, list the use of each item
say why they should take good care of their personal and school items
compose a poem on taking care of personal and school properties
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you take care of personal and school items?
coreCompetencies: Communication: the skill of communication and self-expression is exhibited as learners compose a poem.
values: Responsibility: learners care for personal and school items.

links: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose a poem.

subStrands.name: Holiness

acquire the value of holiness by keeping away from situations that lead to sin

participate in church activities to grow spiritually

read 1Corithinians 14:26 and list activities mentioned in the Bible text

values: Responsibility is exhibited as learners list activities they do in church.

subStrands.name: The Early Church

outcomes.text: name the disciples of Jesus Christ
describe how the early church was started
desire to turn away from sins according to Acts 2:38

learningExperiences: read Matthew 10:1-4 and list the disciples of Jesus Christ
sort the names of the 12 disciples using flash cards
search for the names of the disciples in a word puzzle
watch a video clip on the twelve disciples
read Acts 2:38-41 on how the early church was started
Role-play how the early church was started
repent their sins as guided in Acts 2:38
keyInquiryQuestions: How was the early church started?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: the skill of developing relationships is nurtured as learners carry out activities together such as sorting, searching and role playing.
values: Responsibility: they learn how to take up assigned roles, by following the example of the disciples of Jesus Christ.

links: Mathematics: mathematical skills are applied as learners use flash cards to sort the names of the 12 disciples.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Holy Bible.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners participate in a role play.

subStrands.name: Standing Firm in Faith

outcomes.text: name the city where believers were first called Christians
retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith
list three lessons learnt from the stoning of Stephen
explain why they should not join ungodly groups
utilise the virtue of assertiveness and stand firm in faith

learningExperiences: sing a song related to standing firm in the Christian faith
read Acts 11: 26 and say where believers were first called Christians
identify Antioch, from a Bible map
in groups, read Acts 7: 54-60 and retell the story of Stephen
brainstorm on lessons learnt from the story of Stephen
explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalised groups, groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ
list ways they can stand firm in their Christian faith
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you stand firm in your Christian faith?
Why should you not join ungodly groups?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: the skill of engaging in self-driven tasks is portrayed as learners identify Antioch from the map.
values: Patriotism: learners explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalised groups and groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ.
pcis: Safety and Security: learners explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalised groups, groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ as their Saviour.
Assertiveness: learners say No! to ungodly groups by standing firm in their faith.
links: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing songs.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.
Social Studies skills are applied as learners locate Antioch from the map.

subStrands.name: Self-control

outcomes.text: ractice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23-25
make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit
demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body

learningExperiences: read Galatians 5:23-25
role-play ‘making decisions that portray self-control’
in groups, list choices they make in their day-to- day lives
list things that can defile them e.g. engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse
say how they can avoid defiling their bodies
compose a song on self-control: Galatians 5:23-25
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you practice self- control?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is portrayed as learners list choices they make in their day-to-day lives.
Imagination and creativity: the skill of originality is exhibited as learners role-play ‘making decisions that portray self- control.’
values: Responsibility is inculcated as learners list and avoid things that can defile their bodies.
Integrity: learners exhibit self-discipline by not engaging in acts that can defile them e.g. watching ungodly movies.
pcis: Human sexuality: learners list choices they make in their day-to-day lives concerning sexual purity.
Child care and protection: learners are empowered to exercise self-control by not defiling their bodies.
Alcohol and substance abuse: learners list things that can defile them e.g. drug use and abuse.
links: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing and role play.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.
